acceptance: A no-auto-merge or hold label applied during a mergeability retry blocks merge and no merge API call occurs.
Drafting, closing, changing the target repository/base, moving main/head, or newly failing required checks during the retry refuse or defer the merge as appropriate.
An initially unknown PR that becomes clean with all live preconditions unchanged still merges; behavioral regression tests cover both outcomes.

description:
New defect in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot PR #86, merged 4e518548051506fa0fb793c605eb7effbf82464f. downstream/controller.py merge_gate checks open/draft/hold/base/required checks before waiting for GitHub mergeability. Its MERGEABLE_POLLS loop sleeps 2/4/8 seconds and re-reads the PR but validates only that head SHA is unchanged. If a person applies no-auto-merge during the wait and GitHub then reports clean, merge_gate returns ready and merge_pr can issue the merge mutation despite the hold. The same stale validation applies to draft/open/base state and required checks changing while waiting. Reproduced directly against the merged implementation: first PR read unknown with no labels, second read clean with no-auto-merge, same head; required checks successful; merge_gate returned (ready, []). No real PR was mutated.

Change in the fork: after every mergeability refresh, revalidate all live authority and merge preconditions, and recheck main and required checks after the wait before returning ready. Preserve exact-head merge and existing hold semantics; do not bypass protection or change polling budgets.
